recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore the older active/completed status clarification in current source; future changes about medication-taking state should use MedicationStatement.adherence and related terminology.
issue_request: FHIR-7913 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 clarification asking whether MedicationStatement.status described the medication order/prescription or the compliance/taking statement, since the old definition said it was the state of the statement while the in-progress code definition described a medication still being taken.
initial_application: The Jira resolution said all Pharmacy statuses would be reviewed and updated with the attached spreadsheet, and the Jira comment says the change was fixed as part of tracker 6310 in svn 6552. Git history maps that to d3c2a3a0552f97b710394710badf5ee4e69c0d56, which updated MedicationStatement.status codes, with follow-up commit 31e9678a6e9f698b2828df5d58dc739aad32c602 changing the status definition away from the old state-of-statement wording.
additional_context: MedicationStatement is active in the current build. Later published Pharmacy decisions including FHIR-12011, FHIR-28593, FHIR-32060, and FHIR-39271 changed the model so MedicationStatement.status is record/statement status while MedicationStatement.adherence carries medication-taking semantics.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source defines MedicationStatement.status as recording status, directs medication-taking/adherence semantics to MedicationStatement.adherence, and limits the status CodeSystem to recorded, entered-in-error, and draft.

related_jiras.note: FHIR-7913's Jira comment says its status-code update was applied as part of tracker 6310 in svn 6552.

Later R5 decision made MedicationStatement.status the status of the record, not clinical medication-use status.
Later R5 decision refined MedicationStatement.status values to recorded, entered-in-error, and draft.
Later R5 ballot decision confirmed status is statement status and adherence carries medication-taking semantics.
